messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (prod). p95=1.82s (SLO 1.0s), p99=4.32s (SLO 2.0s). Streaming stalls and tail latency spikes observed. Affected pool: gpu-shared-2. Auto-heuristics flagged IO pressure + cgroup writeback surges.

michael (oncall): taking this. paging oncall. any idea which tenants are hot?

ops-bot: Top noisy tenants in gpu-shared-2 (last 5m): ten-834 (43% tokens, sustained streams), ten-192 (12%), ten-499 (burst). IO writeback rate spiked to 420 MB/s on nvme0n1.

michael (oncall): thanks. sara, lee — can you join? this is customer-facing streaming, need live mitigation ASAP.

lee (runtime): looking at traces, KV cache hitrate dropped for ten-834 and we're seeing repeated preemption and large checkpoint writes. streaming worker queuing up. suspect cgroup blkio throttling + noisy writeback.

sara (infra): on my way. preparing migration window and spare nodes. prelim plan: 1) throttle ten-834 IO weight, 2) migrate long-lived streams off gpu-shared-2 to dedicated fallback pool for critical customers, 3) if that fails, evict/evacuate specific instances.

carla (support): I have an open ticket with customer "BrightCast" complaining about repeated stalls in livestream. I'll notify them we're investigating and may route to a degraded pool.

michael (oncall): execute mitigation 1 and 2 now. prioritize critical-tenants list. lee, can you craft a quick QoS rule?

lee (runtime): applying temp QoS policy for tenant ten-834:
```bash
# bump blkio weight for tenant cgroup (live change)
sudo cgset -r blkio.weight=300 /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/ten-834
# lower background writeback pressure
echo 10 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: Command executed on 4 nodes in gpu-shared-2: blkio.weight set to 300 on ten-834 cgroups. Reported immediate drop in queue depth on nvme0n1.

michael (oncall): good. sara, start routing critical customers off this pool to the dedicated fallback now. command to change route: `redwood route assign --pool dedicated-critical --selector tenant=ten-834`

sara (infra): kicked off migration for ten-834 streams to dedicated-critical. Migration step: create shadow sessions, failover to new pool, then cutover. ETA ~45s per session.

lee (runtime): monitoring streaming tail latency now. p95 dropped from 1.82s -> 1.1s within 70s of QoS change, p99 trending down but still elevated at 2.6s. Some long-lived sessions still stalling during checkpoint window.

carla (support): notifying BrightCast: "We're applying temporary routing and QoS changes to reduce stalls. You may see a brief reconnect as we migrate streams. We'll update once stable." :thumbsup:

michael (oncall): if p99 doesn't go under 2.0 in next 3 minutes, we do tenant eviction for non-critical containers. lee, can you identify biggest remaining offenders?

lee (runtime): remaining top offenders: ten-499 (burst writeback), several ephemeral jobs from ten-192. Suggest throttling ten-499 background IO and temporarily draining ephemeral pods.

sara (infra): starting controlled eviction for non-critical containers on gpu-shared-2 (dry-run first). commands: `redwood node drain --pool gpu-shared-2 --filter 'tenant in (ten-499,ten-192) AND critical=false' --grace 30s`

ops-bot: Dry-run shows 18 tasks eligible for immediate eviction; estimated improvement in IO writeback ~120MB/s.

michael (oncall): proceed with eviction. carla, please prep customer comms for any customers whose sessions are force-terminated.

carla (support): on it. I'll tag customers and send templated note with incident id 3420001111.

lee (runtime): eviction in progress... most ephemeral jobs terminated and restarted on other pools. Observed p99 drop -> 1.9s after eviction completed. p95 stable ~0.98s.

michael (oncall): phew. looks like tail improved. keep monitoring for 15m. sara, leave migration in place for ten-834 for now and schedule a follow-up to move them to dedicated capacity if this recurs.

sara (infra): will do. I'll spin up 2 reserved nodes as a safety buffer and open a ticket to discuss reserved capacity with BrightCast.

ops-bot: Incident state: MITIGATED -> partial routing + cgroup QoS + eviction. Current p95=0.98s, p99=1.92s. IO on nvme0n1 dropped to 180 MB/s.

michael (oncall): handing over to postmortem. folks for action items:
- lee: collect trace slices & KV cache metrics across all affected sessions, create repro dataset.
- sara: investigate root cause of writeback spike and whether node-level tuning prevented this.
- infra/product: review tenant admission/QoS defaults and escalations for multi-tenant pools.
- carla: update customers impacted and track any follow-up support tickets.

carla (support): noted. I'll gather affected customer list and open follow-ups.

lee (runtime): will upload traces to /incidents/3420001111 and share eval prompts for regression detection.

michael (oncall): thanks team. creating PM with timeline and actions, moving thread to #postmortems and #incidents-summary when doc ready. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident channel update: please add any logs or screenshots to the incident doc. Incident closed for paging; postmortem required."
